memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the top of the
mountain. So Moses went up and the LORD said to him, 'Go down and warn the
people so they do not force their way through to see the LORD and many of them
perish.'" - Ex 19:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's concern is that people might "force their way through to see the LORD."

That phrase is revealing. Despite the fire and the smoke and the boundary, God
anticipates that curiosity will pull them forward. Human beings want to see. We
push against limits.

Notice that God's warning is protective. He is not guarding His privacy. He is
guarding their lives. The danger is real, and He says so in advance.

There is something in us that resists God's limits, assuming they are arbitrary
or withholding. That suspicion goes right back to the garden, where the serpent's
question was essentially: is God keeping something good from you? (Gen 3:1-5).

The limits God gives are almost always protective. He knows what we can bear and
what would destroy us. A parent's rules about the road are not restrictions on
joy.

Notice also poor Moses. He has just come up, and immediately he is sent down
again. Verse 24 will send him up once more. There is a lot of climbing in this
chapter, and no complaint recorded.

Faithfulness often looks like doing the same journey again because you were
asked.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which of God's limits do you quietly resent?
2. Are you willing to do a tiring thing again simply because God asked?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me to trust that Your limits protect me. Give me willingness for the
repeated, unglamorous obedience. Amen.
